items.title: Why tokenise real world assets?
items.lead: Tokenising records who owns an asset as digital tokens and lets the asset's rules be written into code.

items: Separate record systems
Australian bond trades can take 2 to 4 business days
Breaches often found after the trade

items: One shared record

Each trade checked against fund rules first

facts.claim: Definition of tokenisation
facts.quote: Tokenisation records ownership of financial products and services as digital tokens, and lets you program the rules of the asset.

facts.claim: Records often sit on separate systems
facts.quote: the asset record, the payment instruction, and the legal documentation typically live on different systems operated by different institutions

facts.claim: In Australia, a bond trade can take 2 to 4 business days to settle
facts.quote: A corporate bond trade in Australia can be agreed on a screen in seconds, yet take two to four business days to settle

facts.claim: Rule breaches are often found after the trade
facts.quote: Breaches are often identified after the trade, when remediation is slow and costly.

facts.quote: Establish digital registries as a shared source of truth across issuers, managers, and investors.

facts.quote: each trade is checked against your fund's rules before execution

facts.claim: Tokeniser lists fractional ownership and 24/7 secondary trading for holders

items.title: DBFT consensus
items.lead: Redbelly's nodes, the computers that run it, agree on new blocks together with no leader. Confirmed means final.

left.title: Classic blockchains
items: Nodes compete. One block wins and the rest are wasted.

right.title: DBFT
items: Nodes combine their proposals into one superblock.

items.note: Cannot fork. Proven correct by model checking. Over 97,500 transactions per second in production.

items.title: Receptor
items.lead: Redbelly's built-in identity system. It checks that everyone on the network is who they say they are.

nodes.label: Verifier
nodes.sub: Sets the rules, checks the claims

items.note: Issuers that grant network access must be accredited. Built on the W3C verifiable credential standard.

facts.claim: Receptor is Redbelly's identity protocol and checks participants are who they say they are
facts.quote: Receptor is Redbelly's native digital identity and verifiable credential protocol. It facilitates network access, ensuring that all network participants are who they say they are

facts.claim: Issuer module
facts.quote: Issuer: Use to define and issue verifiable credentials to users.

facts.claim: Holder module
facts.quote: Holder: Use to create experiences for users to store, manage, and use credentials that are issued to them.

facts.claim: Verifier module
facts.quote: Verifier: Use to define eligibility criteria, surface requests of those criteria to users, and verify the authenticity and validity of the claims made by users

facts.claim: Issuers that provide network access are accredited
facts.quote: Redbelly ensures that all issuers who provide network access are accredited

facts.claim: Built on the W3C standard
facts.quote: Receptor is built on the W3C verifiable credential data model

items.title: Verifiable credentials
items.lead: A digital proof about you, such as your age or country, signed by a trusted issuer and kept in your wallet.
items.note: Your data stays with you instead of being copied to every service, and one KYC credential can be reused.

facts.claim: Proves age, address or investor status
facts.quote: It allows your users to prove they meet certain criteria (like proving their age, address, or accredited investor status) without having to reveal sensitive personal data.

facts.claim: Signed by a trusted issuer, checked with the issuer's public key
facts.quote: The proof is sent to a verifier service, which checks its mathematical validity against the trusted issuer's public key.

facts.claim: Kept in your wallet
facts.quote: ensuring sensitive data never leaves the user's wallet

facts.claim: Country as an example claim
facts.quote: The verifier requests one or more fields from the user (e.g., "name", "country").

facts.claim: Data stays with you, not copied to every service
facts.quote: user data is kept at the edge and is not duplicated across each service provider

facts.claim: KYC credentials can be reused
facts.quote: Reusable client identity and KYC credentials streamline onboarding and reduce duplication

phone.lead: A signed digital proof about you, kept in your own wallet.

items.title: Zero knowledge (ZK) proofs
items.lead: A way to prove something is true without showing the data behind it.

left.title: Selective Disclosure
items: Reveals only the field asked for, such as the birth date

right.title: Proof by Query
items: Answers true or false. No personal data is revealed.

items.note: On chain, a smart contract checks the proof. Useful for conditions such as voting in a DAO.
items.footer: docs.redbelly.network, page: Selective Disclosure vs. Proof by Query

facts.claim: Definition of a zero knowledge proof
facts.quote: Proof by Query (PBQ) uses zero-knowledge proofs, allow users to prove a statement is true without revealing any of the underlying data that makes it true.

facts.claim: Example question over 18
facts.quote: The verifier asks a yes/no question using a query, like “Is the user over 18?”

facts.claim: Selective Disclosure reveals only requested fields, off chain
facts.quote: Selective Disclosure (SD) is a method where a user reveal only specific fields from their credential to a verifier. This process is handled off-chain

facts.claim: Birth date as the revealed field
facts.quote: a user can reveal that the birth date on their passport is 01/01/1994 without disclosing the rest of the details of their passport

facts.claim: Proof by Query result is true or false with no personal data
facts.quote: The result is a simple "true" or "false," with no personal data ever being exposed on-chain.

facts.claim: A smart contract checks the proof on chain
facts.quote: For on-chain the proof is submitted to the blockchain, where a smart contract verifies its validity.

facts.claim: Voting in a DAO as a use
facts.quote: You want to verify a condition (such as voting in a DAO, participating in a token sale, or accessing a DeFi protocol).

phone.lead: Prove something is true without showing the data behind it.

items: Reveals only the field asked for

items.title: Identity and accountability

layers.label: Proofs of fraud

items.note: In Project Acacia, participants verified their identity while zero knowledge proofs kept their privacy.

facts.claim: Identity verified through accredited credential issuers

facts.claim: Nodes that try to cause disagreement leave signed traces that honest nodes combine into proofs of fraud
facts.quote: When faulty nodes try to cause disagreement, they leave cryptographically signed traces that honest nodes can combine to build undeniable proofs of fraud

facts.quote: This process involves an exclusion protocol to remove the identified faulty nodes from the consensus committee

facts.claim: Research project led by the RBA and the DFCRC on digital money for tokenised asset markets
facts.quote: Project Acacia is a research initiative led by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) and the Digital Finance Cooperative Research Centre (DFCRC). Its goal is to explore how different forms of digital money and supporting infrastructure could help develop wholesale tokenised asset markets in Australia.

facts.claim: 24 use cases selected
facts.quote: 24 innovative use cases from a diverse range of organisations

facts.claim: 19 with real money
facts.quote: 19 pilot use cases, which will involve real money and real asset transactions

facts.claim: July 2025 announcement

facts.claim: Pilot wholesale CBDC issued on Redbelly and other platforms
facts.quote: Issuance of pilot wholesale CBDC for testing use cases will occur on a range of private and public-permissioned DLT platforms, including Hedera, Redbelly Network, R3 Corda and other EVM-compatible networks.

facts.claim: CBDC means central bank digital currency
facts.quote: pilot wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC)

facts.claim: Used Redbelly's mainnet
facts.quote: The RBA will mint a limited amount of wholesale CBDC directly onto the Redbelly mainnet

facts.claim: A tokenised corporate bond settled
facts.quote: It has settled a tokenised corporate bond in the Reserve Bank of Australia's pilot wholesale CBDC as part of Project Acacia.
